title: Code is run from text with eval()
description: The code calls eval(), which turns a piece of text into running program code at runtime.
impact: If any part of that text can be influenced by a user, they can run their own commands inside your app and read or change anything it can reach.

remediation.summary: Remove eval() and express the logic directly in code.
steps: Find what the text passed to eval() is meant to do.
Rewrite it as ordinary functions, a lookup table or JSON.parse for data.
Delete the eval() call.

howToConfirmFixed: Search the app for 'eval(' and confirm there are no matches; re-run the static scan.

title: Code is built from text with new Function()
description: The code uses new Function(...), which compiles text into a function at runtime, the same risk as eval().
impact: Text that reaches that call can become arbitrary code running with the app's full permissions.

remediation.summary: Replace new Function() with a normal function or a data lookup.
steps: Identify the text being compiled.
Write the behaviour as a regular function or map of allowed operations.
Remove the new Function() call.

howToConfirmFixed: Search for 'new Function' and confirm no matches; re-run the static scan.

title: The vm module runs dynamic code
description: The code imports node:vm to run scripts at runtime. The vm module is not a security sandbox.
impact: A script that reaches vm can escape and run with the app's full permissions.

remediation.summary: Remove the vm usage; implement the behaviour in ordinary code.
steps: Identify why dynamic scripts are run.
Replace with fixed functions selected by validated input.
Remove the import of node:vm.

howToConfirmFixed: Search for "node:vm" and 'vm' imports and confirm no matches.

title: The app runs operating system commands
description: The code uses child_process (exec, spawn, execSync) to run commands on the computer.
impact: Commands run with the app's operating system permissions. A mistake in how the command is built can let a user run their own commands, and the generated app's design forbids this.

remediation.summary: Remove the system command and use a Node.js library or built-in function instead.
steps: Identify what the command does (for example resizing an image or listing files).
Replace it with node:fs or another allowed built-in module.
Remove the child_process import.

howToConfirmFixed: Search for 'child_process' and confirm there are no matches.

title: User input reaches an operating system command
description: A value that came from a request is used inside a system command.
impact: Anyone who can send that request can run arbitrary commands on the computer running the app: read files, install software, delete data.

remediation.summary: Never pass user input to a shell. Remove the command entirely or use a library.
steps: Remove the child_process call.
Implement the operation with a Node.js built-in or allowed library.
If a command is unavoidable, use execFile with a fixed program and an allow-listed argument set, never a shell string.

howToConfirmFixed: Search for 'child_process' and confirm no matches; the static scan reports nothing.

title: Database query built by joining text
description: A SQL statement is assembled by adding user-provided text into the query string instead of using placeholders.
impact: A user can type special characters that change the query (SQL injection) to read, change or delete any data in the database, including other people's records and password hashes.

remediation.summary: Use placeholders (?) with the db helpers and pass values separately.
steps: Find the query that uses + or a template string with a variable.
Replace each variable in the SQL text with ? and pass the values as the params array.
Keep column and table names fixed in code; never take them from input.

howToConfirmFixed: Re-run the static scan; the dast.input.sql-smoke probe passes; a test sends ' OR 1=1-- and gets no extra rows.

title: Database accessed outside the db helpers
description: Code opens or queries the SQLite database directly instead of going through src/db/index.ts.
impact: The helpers enforce parameterised queries, transactions and file permissions. Bypassing them makes injection and inconsistent data more likely and hides the access from the security checks.

remediation.summary: Route every query through db.q / db.get / db.all / db.run / withTransaction.
steps: Remove the direct node:sqlite import.
Import the helpers from src/db/index.ts.
Rewrite the query with ? placeholders.

howToConfirmFixed: Search for 'node:sqlite' outside src/db and confirm no matches.

title: Unescaped output in a page template
description: A template uses <%- ... %>, which inserts a value into the page without making it safe, and the value is not the nonce or CSRF token.
impact: If the value contains text a user typed, that text can include a script that runs in every visitor's browser (cross-site scripting), stealing sessions or performing actions as them.

remediation.summary: Use <%= %> so EJS escapes the value.
steps: Change <%- value %> to <%= value %>.
If you truly need HTML, build it from fixed strings in code and wrap with safeHtml(), never from user data.
remediation.example:
<%- note.body %>

<%= note.body %>

howToConfirmFixed: The static scan reports no <%- usage; dast.xss.stored-smoke and dast.xss.reflected-smoke pass.

title: Inline script without the CSP nonce
description: A template contains a <script> tag without nonce="<%= nonce %>".
impact: The browser will block the script under the app's Content Security Policy, so the feature breaks; and if someone relaxes the policy to make it work, injected scripts would run too.

remediation.summary: Move the script into public/js/features/ and load it with the nonce.
steps: Create public/js/features/<name>.js with the script contents.
Reference it from the template with <script nonce="<%= nonce %>" src="/js/features/<name>.js"></script>.
Remove the inline script.
remediation.example:
<!-- After -->
<script nonce="<%= nonce %>" src="/js/features/booking.js"></script>

howToConfirmFixed: The page works with no CSP errors in the browser console; the static scan reports nothing.

title: Inline event handler attribute
description: An element uses an attribute like onclick="..." to run code.
impact: Inline handlers are blocked by the Content Security Policy and encourage mixing data with code, which leads to script injection.

remediation.summary: Attach handlers from a script file with addEventListener.
steps: Give the element an id or data attribute.
In public/js/features/<name>.js, select it and call addEventListener.
Remove the on* attribute.
remediation.example:
// public/js/features/notes.js
document.querySelector('[data-action="delete"]').addEventListener('click', onDelete);

howToConfirmFixed: Search templates for 'on[a-z]+=' and confirm no matches.

title: HTML set from data with innerHTML
description: Browser code assigns a value to element.innerHTML.
impact: If the value contains user-provided text, a script inside it runs in the visitor's browser.

remediation.summary: Use textContent for text, or build elements with createElement.
steps: Replace innerHTML = value with textContent = value for plain text.
For structured content, create elements with document.createElement and set their textContent.

howToConfirmFixed: Search public/js for innerHTML and confirm no matches.

title: document.write used
description: Browser code calls document.write, which injects raw HTML into the page.
impact: Any user-controlled text written this way can run as script.

remediation.summary: Replace document.write with DOM methods that set text.
steps: Create the element with document.createElement.
Set its textContent and append it.

howToConfirmFixed: Search public/js for document.write and confirm no matches.

title: React dangerouslySetInnerHTML used
description: A React component renders raw HTML with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
impact: User text rendered this way can contain scripts that run in other users' browsers.

remediation.summary: Render text as children instead of raw HTML.
steps: Replace dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: value}} with {value} as element content.
If HTML is essential, sanitise it with a maintained library first.

howToConfirmFixed: Search for dangerouslySetInnerHTML and confirm no matches.

title: Link address taken from data without a protocol check
description: An href is set from a stored or user-provided value without checking it starts with http:// or https://.
impact: A value like javascript:... runs code when clicked.

remediation.summary: Only allow http and https links; otherwise render plain text.
steps: Parse the value with new URL() and check protocol is http: or https:.
Fall back to showing the text without a link.

howToConfirmFixed: A stored value of javascript:alert(1) renders as text, not a link.

title: postMessage listener does not check the sender
description: A 'message' event listener processes data without checking event.origin.
impact: Any website open in the same browser can send messages that the app will act on.

remediation.summary: Check event.origin against the app's own origin before using the data.
steps: Compare event.origin === window.location.origin.
Validate the message shape before acting on it.

howToConfirmFixed: The listener returns early for foreign origins; a test posts from a different origin and nothing happens.

title: Weak hash (MD5/SHA-1) used for a security value
description: MD5 or SHA-1 is used on something named like a token, password or session.
impact: These hashes are broken; attackers can find collisions or reverse short values, weakening the protection the hash was meant to give.

remediation.summary: Use SHA-256 (or HMAC-SHA256 with a key) for tokens; use the password helpers for passwords.
steps: Replace createHash('md5'|'sha1') with createHash('sha256') or createHmac('sha256', config.tokenHmacKey).
For passwords, use hashPassword/verifyPassword from src/security/password.ts.
remediation.example:
import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto';
const tokenHash = createHmac('sha256', config.tokenHmacKey).update(token).digest('hex');

howToConfirmFixed: Search for md5 and sha1 and confirm no matches in security code.

title: Math.random used for a security value
description: Math.random() generates a token, id, code or password.
impact: Math.random is predictable. Tokens made from it can be guessed, letting attackers take over sessions or reset links.

remediation.summary: Use crypto.randomBytes or crypto.randomUUID.
steps: Replace Math.random with randomBytes(32).toString('base64url') for tokens.
Use randomInt for numeric codes.
remediation.example:
import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';
const token = randomBytes(32).toString('base64url');

howToConfirmFixed: Search for Math.random and confirm it is only used for non-security purposes such as animations.

title: Deprecated createCipher used
description: The code uses crypto.createCipher / createDecipher, which derive keys weakly and use no random IV.
impact: Encrypted data can be attacked because the same input always produces the same output and the key derivation is weak.

remediation.summary: Use the template's encryptField/decryptField (AES-256-GCM) instead.
steps: Remove createCipher calls.
Mark the field as sensitive in the entity definition so the CRUD layer encrypts it, or call encryptField(table, column, rowId, value) directly.
remediation.example:
import { encryptField, decryptField } from '../../db/field-crypto.ts';
const stored = encryptField('patients', 'diagnosis', row.id, diagnosis);

howToConfirmFixed: Search for createCipher( and confirm no matches; tests named V11.3.2 pass.

title: Secret written directly in the code
description: A password, API key or signing secret appears as a literal string in a source file.
impact: Anyone who sees the code (backups, sharing, version control) gets the secret, and it cannot be rotated without changing code.

remediation.summary: Move the secret to the environment and read it through config.
steps: Delete the literal from the code.
Add a variable to .env (and a placeholder to .env.example).
Read it via the typed config object.
Rotate the exposed secret, since it must be considered leaked.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan and static scan report nothing; the old secret has been revoked.

title: Certificate checking disabled
description: The code sets rejectUnauthorized: false or NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, turning off certificate verification for outbound connections.
impact: Anyone on the network path can impersonate the service the app talks to and read or alter the data, including API keys sent to it.

remediation.summary: Remove the override and use outboundFetch, which validates certificates.
steps: Delete rejectUnauthorized: false and any NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED assignment.
If a self-signed internal service is unavoidable, add its CA certificate via NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS instead.
remediation.example:
import { outboundFetch } from '../../lib/http-client.ts';
const res = await outboundFetch('https://api.example.com/v1/items', { method: 'GET' });

howToConfirmFixed: Search for rejectUnauthorized and NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED and confirm no matches.

title: CORS allows any site with credentials
description: Cross-origin sharing is configured with origin '*' (or reflected) together with credentials allowed.
impact: Any website can make your visitors' browsers call the app with their session and read the responses.

remediation.summary: Remove the CORS configuration; the app does not need cross-origin access.
steps: Delete the CORS middleware or headers.
If another site genuinely needs access, use a fixed allow-list of origins and never combine '*' with credentials.

howToConfirmFixed: dast.cors.origin-not-reflected passes; no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header appears.

title: CORS allows any site
description: Cross-origin sharing is configured with origin '*'.
impact: Other websites can read responses from your app in a visitor's browser, which may expose data that should stay private.

remediation.summary: Remove the CORS configuration or restrict it to a fixed list of origins.
steps: Delete the wildcard CORS header.
If needed, compare the Origin header to a fixed allow-list and echo only exact matches.
remediation.example: // Remove: res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*');

howToConfirmFixed: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header appears in responses.

title: Cookie set without HttpOnly
description: A cookie is set without the HttpOnly flag.
impact: Page scripts can read the cookie; if a script injection ever happens, the cookie (possibly a session) can be stolen.

remediation.summary: Set httpOnly: true on every cookie, or use the session helpers.
steps: Add httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'strict', secure (in TLS modes) to res.cookie options.
Prefer storing state in the session rather than extra cookies.
remediation.example: res.cookie('prefs', value, { httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'strict', secure: config.tlsMode !== 'off', path: '/' });

howToConfirmFixed: dast.cookie.session-attributes passes and every Set-Cookie header shows HttpOnly.

title: Cookie set without SameSite
description: A cookie is set without a SameSite attribute.
impact: Browsers may send the cookie on requests started by other sites, which helps cross-site request forgery.

remediation.summary: Set sameSite: 'strict' (or 'lax') on the cookie.
steps: Add sameSite: 'strict' to the res.cookie options.
remediation.example: res.cookie('prefs', value, { httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'strict', path: '/' });

howToConfirmFixed: Every Set-Cookie header includes SameSite.

title: Content Security Policy disabled
description: helmet is configured with contentSecurityPolicy: false or the CSP directives were relaxed with 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval'.
impact: The browser will run injected scripts, removing the last line of defence against cross-site scripting.

remediation.summary: Restore the template's nonce-based policy from src/security/headers.ts.
steps: Remove the contentSecurityPolicy: false option or the unsafe directives.
Move inline scripts to public/js/features/ and load them with the nonce.
remediation.example: app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: { directives: buildCspDirectives } }));

howToConfirmFixed: dast.headers.csp passes with the exact policy.

title: Regular expression can run extremely slowly
description: A regular expression has nested repetition (for example (a+)+) that can take exponential time on crafted input.
impact: A short specially crafted input can make the server freeze for seconds or minutes, blocking everyone else (denial of service).

remediation.summary: Simplify the pattern and cap the input length.
steps: Rewrite the pattern without nested quantifiers or overlapping alternatives.
Validate input length with the zod schema before matching.
Consider a simple string check instead of a regex.

howToConfirmFixed: The static scan reports nothing and a long input of repeated characters responds instantly.

title: Regular expression built from user input
description: new RegExp() is built from a value that came from a request.
impact: A user can supply a pattern that runs for a very long time (denial of service) or matches more than intended.

remediation.summary: Escape the input or replace the regex with a plain string comparison.
steps: Use String.prototype.includes or startsWith for searches.
If a pattern is needed, escape special characters first and cap the length.
remediation.example:
const term = req.valid.query.q; // validated max length
const rows = db.all('SELECT id, title FROM notes WHERE owner_id = ? AND title LIKE ? LIMIT 50', [req.user.id, `%${term.replace(/[%_]/g, '')}%`]);

howToConfirmFixed: No RegExp is built from request data.

title: File path built from user input
description: path.join or path.resolve is called with a value from a request.
impact: A value like ../../.env lets a user read or write files outside the intended folder, including secrets.

remediation.summary: Look files up by internal id and never use user text in a path.
steps: Store files under random ids (the uploads module does this).
Resolve the path from the database record, not from the request.
If a name must be used, allow only [a-z0-9-] and verify the resolved path starts with the base directory.
remediation.example:
const upload = await uploads.getOwned(req.user, req.valid.params.id);
const filePath = path.join(config.dataDir, 'uploads', upload.id); // id is a uuid from the DB

howToConfirmFixed: dast.input.path-traversal-smoke passes; the static scan reports nothing.

title: File read or written at a user-controlled path
description: A node:fs call receives a path that includes request data.
impact: Users can read or overwrite arbitrary files the app can access, such as the database or .env.

remediation.summary: Only access files through the uploads module or fixed paths.
steps: Remove direct fs access from feature code.
Use the uploads feature (store/get/delete) which validates ownership and uses generated names.

howToConfirmFixed: Search feature code for node:fs and confirm no matches outside src/lib and src/features/uploads.

title: Redirect target taken from the request
description: res.redirect is called with a value from req.query, req.body or req.params.
impact: A link to your app can bounce users to a look-alike site that steals their password, and the link looks trustworthy because it starts with your address.

remediation.summary: Use safeRedirect with an allow-list of local paths.
steps: Replace res.redirect(target) with safeRedirect(res, target, ['/dashboard', '/notes']).
Default to a fixed path when the target is not allowed.
remediation.example:
import { safeRedirect } from '../../security/redirect.ts';
safeRedirect(res, req.valid.query.next, ['/', '/notes']);

howToConfirmFixed: dast.redirect.open-redirect-blocked passes.

title: Whole database row sent to the client
description: res.json or res.render receives a raw database row instead of a shaped DTO.
impact: Internal or private columns (owner ids, hashes, encrypted blobs, notes meant for admins) leak to users who should not see them.

remediation.summary: Pass rows through the entity's toPublicDto / toOwnerDto / toAdminDto.
steps: Define the DTO functions in the feature module using pick() from src/lib/dto.ts.
Choose the DTO by the requester's role.
Return the DTO, never the row.

howToConfirmFixed: API responses contain only DTO fields; tests named V15.3.1 pass.

title: Request body used without validation
description: A handler reads req.body directly instead of req.valid.body from a defineRoute schema.
impact: Unexpected types, missing fields and extra fields reach your logic, enabling mass assignment, crashes and injection.

remediation.summary: Declare a strict zod body schema in defineRoute and read req.valid.body.
steps: Add schema: { body: z.object({...}).strict() } to the route spec.
Replace req.body with req.valid.body.

howToConfirmFixed: Search for req.body in feature code and confirm no matches; dast.input.unknown-field passes.

title: Route registered without defineRoute
description: A route is added with app.get / router.post directly instead of defineRoute.
impact: The route skips the registry's mandatory authorization declaration, validation, CSRF and rate-limit defaults, so it may be reachable by anyone.

remediation.summary: Register every route through defineRoute with an explicit auth value.
steps: Replace router.<method>(path, handler) with defineRoute(router, { method, path, auth, schema }, handler).
Add the route to routes.manifest.json.
remediation.example: defineRoute(router, { method: 'GET', path: '/notes/:id', auth: 'user', owner: { entity: 'note', param: 'id' }, schema: { params: IdParams } }, handler);

howToConfirmFixed: The startup check assertAllRoutesRegistered passes; dast.authz.unregistered-route passes.

title: Route has no authorization declaration
description: A defineRoute call has no auth value.
impact: Without an explicit rule the route's access is undefined; it may be open to anyone including signed-out visitors.

remediation.summary: Set auth to 'public', 'user' or 'role:<name>' deliberately.
steps: Decide who should use the route.
Add auth (and owner for per-record access).
Write a test that anonymous and wrong-role users are denied.
remediation.example: defineRoute(router, { method: 'DELETE', path: '/api/notes/:id', auth: 'user', owner: { entity: 'note', param: 'id' } }, handler);

howToConfirmFixed: dast.authz.anonymous-denied and dast.authz.wrong-role-denied pass for the route.

title: fetch() used outside the HTTP client
description: Code calls the global fetch directly instead of outboundFetch from src/lib/http-client.ts.
impact: The call bypasses the outbound allow-list, timeouts, size cap and redirect control, so a user-influenced address could reach internal services (server-side request forgery).

remediation.summary: Use outboundFetch and add the host to OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_HOSTS.
steps: Import outboundFetch.
Add the destination host to OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_HOSTS in .env and .env.example.
Never build the URL from user input.
remediation.example:
import { outboundFetch } from '../../lib/http-client.ts';
const res = await outboundFetch('https://api.weather.example/today?city=' + encodeURIComponent(city));

howToConfirmFixed: Search for 'fetch(' outside src/lib/http-client.ts and confirm no matches.

title: node:http/https request outside the HTTP client
description: Code uses http.request or https.get directly.
impact: Same as direct fetch: the allow-list, timeout and size limits are bypassed.

remediation.summary: Replace with outboundFetch.
steps: Remove the node:http/https import.
Use outboundFetch with the allow-listed host.
remediation.example: const res = await outboundFetch('https://api.example.com/v1/status');

howToConfirmFixed: Search for 'node:http' and 'node:https' outside src/lib and src/server.ts and confirm no matches.

title: User input in an email header
description: A value from a request is placed in an email subject, To, From or other header without sanitisation.
impact: Line breaks in the value can add extra recipients or headers, turning your app into a spam relay or leaking messages.

remediation.summary: Use the mailer's sendMail with validated fields; it strips header line breaks.
steps: Validate the address with z.string().email() and the subject with a max length.
Pass values to mailer.sendMail rather than composing headers by hand.
remediation.example: await mailer.sendMail({ to: req.valid.body.email, template: 'booking-confirmed', data: { name } });

howToConfirmFixed: Tests named V1.3.11 pass; a subject containing a newline is rejected.

title: Request data copied wholesale into a record
description: Object.assign or a spread copies req.body (or a whole request object) into a database row or model.
impact: Users can set fields they should not control, such as owner id, role or price (mass assignment).

remediation.summary: Copy only the fields the action allows, from the validated body.
steps: Use a strict zod schema so unknown fields are rejected.
Assign fields explicitly: { title, body } = req.valid.body.
remediation.example:
const { title, body } = req.valid.body;
db.run('UPDATE notes SET title = ?, body = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ?', [title, body, now(), id, req.user.id]);

howToConfirmFixed: A request with an extra field such as ownerId is rejected with 400.

title: Deep merge of untrusted data
description: A recursive merge or a lookup by user-provided key touches __proto__ or constructor.
impact: Crafted input can change the behaviour of every object in the app (prototype pollution), which can bypass checks or crash the app.

remediation.summary: Use Map for dynamic keys and never merge untrusted objects recursively.
steps: Validate input with a strict schema (rejects __proto__).
Replace dynamic-key objects with Map or Object.create(null).
Remove the deep merge.
remediation.example:
const settings = new Map<string, string>();
settings.set(req.valid.body.key, req.valid.body.value);

howToConfirmFixed: dast.input.proto-pollution passes.

title: Sensitive value written to the log
description: A log call includes a password, token, secret, or a field marked sensitive.
impact: Logs are often copied and kept for a long time; a secret in a log is a secret leaked to everyone who can read logs.

remediation.summary: Log identifiers and outcomes, never the sensitive value.
steps: Remove the sensitive field from the log call.
Use events.emit with the catalogued fields; the logger redacts known keys, but do not rely on it.

howToConfirmFixed: Tests named V16.2.5 pass; a search of app.log for the value finds nothing.

title: console.log used instead of the logger
description: Code writes to console.log instead of the structured logger.
impact: Console output is unstructured, bypasses redaction and is easy to lose, so incidents are harder to investigate and secrets may slip out.

remediation.summary: Use logger from src/lib/logger.ts.
steps: Replace console.log with logger.info / logger.warn / logger.error.
Pass structured fields, not concatenated strings.
remediation.example:
import { logger } from '../../lib/logger.ts';
logger.info({ noteId: id }, 'note created');

howToConfirmFixed: Search for console. in src and confirm no matches.

title: Secret falls back to a built-in default
description: Code reads process.env.SOMETHING || 'literal', so a missing environment value silently becomes a known constant.
impact: If the variable is ever unset, the app runs with a secret anyone can read in the code, which is as bad as no secret.

remediation.summary: Read secrets only through config, which refuses to start when they are missing.
steps: Delete the fallback literal.
Add the variable to the config schema in src/config.ts (protected file: ask for it in the design if new) or read an existing config field.

howToConfirmFixed: Search for 'process.env' outside src/config.ts and confirm no fallbacks with ||.

title: Static file serving allows dotfiles
description: express.static is configured with dotfiles: 'allow'.
impact: Hidden files such as .env or .git inside the public folder would be served to anyone.

remediation.summary: Use dotfiles: 'deny' (the template default).
steps: Change the option to dotfiles: 'deny'.
Keep secrets out of the public folder entirely.
remediation.example: app.use(express.static('public', { dotfiles: 'deny', index: false }));

howToConfirmFixed: dast.leak.dotfiles passes.

title: trust proxy set to true
description: app.set('trust proxy', true) trusts every X-Forwarded-* header.
impact: Any visitor can claim any IP address, defeating rate limits, lockouts and audit logs.

remediation.summary: Set trust proxy to the exact number of proxies via TRUST_PROXY_HOPS.
steps: Remove the hard-coded true.
Set TRUST_PROXY_HOPS in .env to the number of proxies (0 when none).
remediation.example: app.set('trust proxy', config.trustProxyHops); // from TRUST_PROXY_HOPS

howToConfirmFixed: dast.rate.xff-spoof-ignored passes and config.trust-proxy-hops passes.

title: Several database writes without a transaction
description: A handler performs two or more writes without withTransaction.
impact: If the second write fails, the first stays, leaving inconsistent data (for example a booking without its payment record).

remediation.summary: Wrap related writes in withTransaction.
steps: Import withTransaction from src/db/index.ts.
Move all writes inside the callback so they succeed or fail together.

howToConfirmFixed: Tests named V2.3.3 pass; the static scan reports nothing.

title: Secret compared with ===
description: A token, hash or secret is compared with === or ==, which stops at the first different character.
impact: By measuring response times an attacker can guess a secret one character at a time.

remediation.summary: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers.
steps: Hash both values (or ensure equal length) and compare with timingSafeEqual.
For passwords use verifyPassword; for tokens compare HMACs.

howToConfirmFixed: No === comparisons remain on values named token/secret/hash.

title: JWT accepts the 'none' algorithm
description: A JSON Web Token library is used with algorithm 'none' or without an algorithm allow-list.
impact: Anyone can forge a token that the app accepts as a signed-in user or administrator.

remediation.summary: Do not use JWTs in this app; use the session store or API keys.
steps: Remove the JWT library usage (it is not in allowedImports).
Use the built-in session for users and the apikeys feature for machine access.
remediation.example:
// Use sessions: req.user is populated by the session middleware
if (!req.user) return forbid(res);

howToConfirmFixed: Search for jsonwebtoken/jose and confirm no matches.

title: Secret question or password hint field
description: A form or table has a field for a password hint or security question.
impact: Answers to questions like 'mother's maiden name' are easy to find, giving attackers a way around the password.

remediation.summary: Remove hints and secret questions; use the email reset flow and MFA recovery codes.
steps: Delete the field from the form, schema and migration.
Rely on the built-in password reset and recovery codes.
remediation.example: // Remove: securityQuestion, securityAnswer, passwordHint fields

howToConfirmFixed: Tests named V6.4.2 pass; the fields no longer exist.

title: Password composition rule added
description: Code requires uppercase, digits or symbols in passwords.
impact: Composition rules push people toward predictable patterns (Password1!) and block long passphrases; length and a common-password check protect better.

remediation.summary: Remove the composition rule and keep the template policy (12+ characters, common-password check).
steps: Delete the character-class check.
Use validatePassword from src/security/password.ts.
remediation.example:
import { validatePassword } from '../../security/password.ts';
const problem = validatePassword(candidate, { email, name, appName: config.appName });

howToConfirmFixed: Tests named V6.2.5 pass.

title: XML parser allows external entities
description: An XML parser is used with external entity resolution enabled (or an XML library is used at all in this app).
impact: A crafted XML file can make the server read local files (like .env) or contact internal services.

remediation.summary: Avoid XML; if unavoidable, disable external entities and DTDs.
steps: Prefer JSON input validated with zod.
If XML is required, configure the parser with entity processing off.
remediation.example:
// Prefer JSON:
schema: { body: ImportSchema.strict() }

howToConfirmFixed: No XML parser is imported, or entity resolution is explicitly disabled.

title: Untrusted data deserialised into objects
description: A library such as node-serialize or a custom unserialize turns request data into live objects.
impact: Serialized payloads can contain code that runs when unpacked, giving full control of the app.

remediation.summary: Accept JSON only and validate it with zod.
steps: Remove the deserialisation library.
Use JSON.parse (Express does this for application/json) followed by a strict schema.
remediation.example: const data = ImportSchema.strict().parse(req.valid.body);

howToConfirmFixed: Search for serialize/unserialize libraries and confirm no matches.

title: AI answer inserted into a page without escaping
description: Text from the AI assistant is rendered with <%- %> , innerHTML or a Markdown-to-HTML converter.
impact: A manipulated AI answer (for example through injected instructions in a record) could contain a script that runs in users' browsers.

remediation.summary: Render AI answers as escaped plain text.
steps: Use <%= answer %> in the template (line breaks can be preserved with CSS white-space: pre-wrap).
Do not convert Markdown to HTML.
remediation.example: <%= answer %>

howToConfirmFixed: dast.ai.output-escaped passes.

title: API key or secret included in an AI prompt
description: A prompt string or tool input contains a config secret or process.env value.
impact: The secret leaves your computer inside the model request and could be echoed back to a user or logged by the provider.

remediation.summary: Keep secrets out of prompts; the SDK reads the key from the environment itself.
steps: Remove the secret from the prompt or tool parameters.
Let the Anthropic client use ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from config internally.
remediation.example:
const client = new Anthropic({ apiKey: config.anthropicApiKey }); // never in messages
const messages = [{ role: 'user', content: wrapUntrusted(userText) }];

howToConfirmFixed: Search src/features/ai for process.env and config secrets inside strings and confirm no matches.

title: Package imported that is not on the allow-list
description: Generated code imports a package outside express, zod, ejs, pino, node:* and the template's own modules.
impact: Unreviewed packages can carry vulnerabilities or malicious code, and the app's locked dependency set no longer describes what runs.

remediation.summary: Remove the import and use an allowed module or template helper.
steps: Find the functionality the package provided.
Replace with a Node.js built-in (node:crypto, node:fs, node:path) or a template helper.
Delete the import.

howToConfirmFixed: Typecheck and the static scan both pass; package.json is unchanged.

title: Sensitive value sent in a URL parameter
description: A route reads a sensitive field (password, token, card number, health data) from the query string or path.
impact: URLs are stored in browser history, server logs and referrer headers, so the value leaks widely.

remediation.summary: Move sensitive values to the request body of a POST route.
steps: Change the route method to POST with a body schema.
Update the form or fetch call to send the value in the body.
remediation.example: defineRoute(router, { method: 'POST', path: '/api/search', auth: 'user', schema: { body: z.object({ nationalId: z.string().max(20) }).strict() } }, handler);

howToConfirmFixed: Tests named V14.2.1 pass; no sensitive names appear in query schemas.

title: Protected security file was changed
description: A file the generator must not touch (security, auth, config, tests/security, manifest) no longer matches its recorded hash.
impact: A security control may have been weakened or removed, and the compliance evidence for the template controls is no longer valid.

remediation.summary: Restore the file from the template and make the change in a writable location instead.
steps: Compare the file with the template version and restore it.
If a change is genuinely needed, treat it as a manual, reviewed edit and re-run the full verification.
remediation.example: // Restore from templates/secure-web-app/<path> and re-run verification

howToConfirmFixed: config.protected-files-unchanged passes.

title: Unfinished security note in the code
description: A TODO or FIXME comment mentions auth, permission, security or validation.
impact: It usually marks a check that was never finished; the protection it describes may not exist.

remediation.summary: Finish or remove the item and record the decision.
steps: Read the comment and implement the missing check, or remove it if already done.
Add a test for the behaviour.
remediation.example: // TODO: check owner -> replace with owner: { entity: 'note', param: 'id' } in the route spec

howToConfirmFixed: The comment is gone and a test covers the behaviour.

title: .env.example is missing
description: The app folder has no .env.example file listing the settings it needs.
impact: Whoever sets the app up next will not know which settings exist and may leave a security setting at an unsafe value.

remediation.summary: Restore .env.example from the template with placeholder values only.
steps: Copy templates/secure-web-app/.env.example into the app folder.
Never put real secrets into .env.example.

howToConfirmFixed: The file exists and contains only placeholders.

title: .gitignore does not exclude .env
description: The .gitignore file does not list .env (and .env.*), so secrets could be committed to version control.
impact: Once a secret is in a repository it is effectively public to everyone with access, including any backup or hosting service.

remediation.summary: Add .env and .env.* to .gitignore and rotate secrets if they were ever committed.
steps: Add the lines .env and .env.* to .gitignore.
If .env was already committed, remove it from history and run npm run setup to generate new secrets.
remediation.example:
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
data/

howToConfirmFixed: git check-ignore .env reports the file is ignored.

title: A secret in .env is weak or a placeholder
description: SESSION_SECRET, FIELD_KEYS or TOKEN_HMAC_KEY is shorter than 32 bytes or equals the .env.example placeholder.
impact: Sessions, reset tokens, API keys and encrypted fields all rely on these values. A weak or known value lets an attacker forge sessions or decrypt data.

remediation.summary: Generate strong secrets with the setup script.
steps: Run npm run setup (or node scripts/gen-secrets.ts) in the app folder.
Restart the app; it refuses to start with weak secrets.
If the app already ran with the weak value, sign everyone out.
remediation.example: npm run setup

howToConfirmFixed: config.secrets-strength passes on the next run.

title: Default administrator credential present
description: An ADMIN_PASSWORD-style variable exists, or FIRST-LOGIN.txt still holds an unused one-time password.
impact: A known or written-down administrator password is the first thing an attacker tries.

remediation.summary: Remove fixed admin passwords; sign in once with the one-time password and delete FIRST-LOGIN.txt.
steps: Delete ADMIN_PASSWORD or similar variables from .env.
Sign in as the bootstrap admin, change the password when prompted, and delete FIRST-LOGIN.txt.

howToConfirmFixed: FIRST-LOGIN.txt is absent and no ADMIN_PASSWORD variable exists.

title: Node.js version not pinned
description: package.json has no engines.node requirement.
impact: Running on an old Node.js version silently loses security fixes and built-in features the app relies on (such as node:sqlite).

remediation.summary: Set engines.node to >=22.13.0.
steps: Restore the engines field in package.json from the template.

howToConfirmFixed: package.json contains the engines field.

title: package-lock.json is missing
description: There is no lockfile, so npm may install different package versions than the ones that were tested.
impact: Untested or compromised versions can be installed without anyone noticing.

remediation.summary: Restore the tested package-lock.json from the template.
steps: Copy package-lock.json from templates/secure-web-app.
Install with npm ci --ignore-scripts.

howToConfirmFixed: package-lock.json exists and npm ci succeeds.

title: npm install scripts are allowed
description: .npmrc does not set ignore-scripts=true.
impact: Packages can run arbitrary code on your computer during install, a common supply-chain attack path.

remediation.summary: Add ignore-scripts=true to .npmrc.
steps: Restore .npmrc from the template (ignore-scripts=true, fund=false, audit=false).
remediation.example:
ignore-scripts=true
fund=false
audit=false

howToConfirmFixed: .npmrc contains ignore-scripts=true.

title: Debug settings enabled
description: NODE_ENV is development, or a start script uses --inspect.
impact: Debug modes show detailed errors and can expose a debugging port that gives full control of the process.

remediation.summary: Run in production mode without inspector flags.
steps: Set NODE_ENV=production (or remove it) in .env.
Remove --inspect from any start command.

howToConfirmFixed: config.no-debug-flags passes; error pages show no stack traces.

title: Example feature enabled in production
description: EXAMPLE_FEATURE=1 mounts the reference 'notes' feature in a production configuration.
impact: Extra functionality nobody uses is still attack surface and clutters your data.

remediation.summary: Set EXAMPLE_FEATURE=0 or remove it from .env.
steps: Edit .env and remove EXAMPLE_FEATURE.
Restart the app.

howToConfirmFixed: The /notes example routes return 404.

title: Test mode enabled in .env
description: SECUREVIBE_TEST_MODE=1 is present in .env.
impact: Test mode seeds known accounts with a known password and exposes helper endpoints. In production that is a ready-made back door.

remediation.summary: Remove SECUREVIBE_TEST_MODE from .env and restart.
steps: Delete the SECUREVIBE_TEST_MODE line from .env.
Restart the app and confirm /__securevibe/routes returns 404.
Delete any seeded @test.local accounts from Admin > Users.

howToConfirmFixed: dast.leak.test-endpoints-absent passes; no @test.local users exist.

title: TLS settings are inconsistent
description: TLS_MODE=proxy but TRUST_PROXY_HOPS is 0, or TLS_MODE=selfsigned but no certificates exist in certs/.
impact: Secure cookies and HSTS may be set wrongly, or the app may fail to start, or think requests are HTTPS when they are not.

remediation.summary: Match TLS_MODE to your setup.
steps: Behind a reverse proxy: TLS_MODE=proxy and TRUST_PROXY_HOPS=1 (or the number of proxies).
Self-signed on the LAN: run npm run gen-cert and set TLS_MODE=selfsigned.
No TLS (this computer only): TLS_MODE=off.

howToConfirmFixed: config.tls-mode-consistent passes and the app starts.

title: Proxy trust setting is wrong
description: TRUST_PROXY_HOPS does not match the deployment (non-zero with no proxy, or zero behind a proxy).
impact: Either visitors can spoof their IP address (too trusting) or every visitor looks like the proxy (rate limits hit everyone at once).

remediation.summary: Set TRUST_PROXY_HOPS to the exact number of proxies in front of the app.
steps: Count the proxies (reverse proxy, load balancer) between the internet and the app.
Set that number in .env and restart.

howToConfirmFixed: dast.rate.xff-spoof-ignored passes and logged IPs are correct.

title: Session timeouts are too long
description: SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES, SESSION_ABSOLUTE_HOURS or SESSION_MAX_CONCURRENT exceed the values documented for the app's level (30/12/5, or 15/8/5 at Level 2).
impact: A session left open on a shared or stolen device stays usable for much longer.

remediation.summary: Restore the documented values in .env.
steps: Set SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES and SESSION_ABSOLUTE_HOURS to the documented values.
Update docs/sessions.md by running npm run docs:build.

howToConfirmFixed: config.session-policy passes and docs/sessions.md matches .env.

title: Protected files differ from the template
description: One or more protected files (security modules, config, security tests, manifest, package files) do not match the hashes recorded at scaffold time.
impact: A control may have been weakened, and the compliance report can no longer credit template controls for those files.

remediation.summary: Restore the changed files from the template or review the change deliberately.
steps: Open the security report to see which files changed.
Restore each from templates/secure-web-app unless you made the change on purpose.
Re-run verification.

howToConfirmFixed: config.protected-files-unchanged passes.

title: Provenance record is missing
description: securevibe.provenance.json is missing or unreadable.
impact: You cannot tell which files were AI-generated, by which model and in which run, which breaks the audit trail.

remediation.summary: Re-run the build so SecureVibe writes provenance, or restore the file from the run folder.
steps: Open pipeline/<runId>/ and restore securevibe.provenance.json into the app folder.
Do not edit it by hand.

howToConfirmFixed: The file exists and config.provenance-present passes.

title: App listens on all network interfaces
description: BIND_LAN=1 is set, so the app accepts connections from other computers on the network.
impact: Anyone on the same network (office Wi-Fi, café) can reach the app. That is fine if intended, but then TLS should be on.

remediation.summary: Keep BIND_LAN=0 unless others on your network need access; if they do, enable TLS.
steps: If only you use the app, remove BIND_LAN from .env.
If your team needs it, keep BIND_LAN=1 and set TLS_MODE=selfsigned (npm run gen-cert) or put it behind a TLS proxy.

howToConfirmFixed: config.bind-loopback-default passes, or TLS is enabled with BIND_LAN.

title: docs/SECURITY.md is missing
description: The security policy document (contact, disclosure, anti-automation settings) is missing.
impact: People who find a problem do not know whom to tell, and the documented controls required by the standard are absent.

remediation.summary: Regenerate the document.
steps: Run npm run docs:build in the app folder.
remediation.example: npm run docs:build

howToConfirmFixed: docs/SECURITY.md exists and names a contact email.

title: README lacks run instructions
description: README.md does not describe how to set up and run the app.
impact: Someone may skip the setup step that generates secrets and creates the first administrator.

remediation.summary: Add a short "How to run" section to README.md with the exact install, setup and start commands for this app.
steps: For an app SecureVibe built, the steps are: npm ci --ignore-scripts, npm run setup, npm start, first login from FIRST-LOGIN.txt.
For any other app, name the commands that install its dependencies and start it, and any setup step that creates secrets or the first account.

howToConfirmFixed: README.md contains the setup and start commands.

title: package.json was modified
description: package.json differs from the tested template version (new dependencies or changed scripts).
impact: New packages were not reviewed or locked; changed scripts may disable checks or enable debug flags.

remediation.summary: Restore package.json from the template and implement the feature with allowed modules.
steps: Compare with templates/secure-web-app/package.json and restore it.
Replace any new package usage with Node.js built-ins.
Run npm ci --ignore-scripts.

howToConfirmFixed: config.package-json-unmodified passes.

title: Anthropic API key found in a file
description: A string starting with sk-ant- (an Anthropic API key) appears in a source or text file.
impact: Anyone with the file can use the key to make paid AI requests on your account and read any data sent to the model.

remediation.summary: Revoke the key in the Anthropic console, create a new one, and keep it only in .env.
steps: Revoke the exposed key at the provider's console.
Create a new key and set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env only.
Delete the key from the file and any copies or backups.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing and the old key no longer works.

title: AWS access key ID found in a file
description: A string like AKIA... (an Amazon Web Services access key id) appears in a file.
impact: Combined with its secret it grants access to your cloud account; keys in files are routinely harvested by attackers.

remediation.summary: Deactivate the key in the AWS console and move credentials out of the code.
steps: Deactivate and delete the key in AWS IAM.
Create a new key if still needed and load it from .env or an instance role.
Remove the value from the file.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing and the key is inactive in IAM.

title: AWS secret access key found in a file
description: A 40-character AWS secret access key is assigned in a file.
impact: Gives full use of the paired access key, that is, access to your cloud account.

remediation.summary: Rotate the key in AWS and remove it from the file.
steps: Deactivate the key pair in AWS IAM.
Create new credentials and load them from .env.
Remove the value from the file.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing.

title: GitHub token found in a file
description: A GitHub personal access token (ghp_, gho_, github_pat_) appears in a file.
impact: Grants access to your repositories, possibly with write permission.

remediation.summary: Revoke the token on GitHub and move it to .env if still needed.
steps: Revoke it under GitHub Settings > Developer settings.
Create a new token with the minimum scopes.
Remove the value from the file.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing and the token is revoked.

title: Slack token found in a file
description: A Slack token (xoxb-, xoxp-, xapp-) appears in a file.
impact: Lets an attacker read or post messages in your Slack workspace as your app or user.

remediation.summary: Revoke the token in Slack and move it to .env.
steps: Revoke it in the Slack app settings.
Issue a new token and store it in .env only.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing.

title: Stripe key found in a file
description: A Stripe key (sk_live_, sk_test_, rk_live_) appears in a file.
impact: A live secret key allows charges and refunds on your Stripe account.

remediation.summary: Roll the key in the Stripe dashboard and keep the new one in .env.
steps: Roll the key in Stripe > Developers > API keys.
Store the new key in .env as STRIPE_SECRET_KEY.
Remove the value from the file.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing and the old key is rolled.

title: Google API key found in a file
description: A Google API key (AIza...) appears in a file.
impact: Can run up charges on your Google Cloud account and access the APIs it is enabled for.

remediation.summary: Regenerate the key in Google Cloud and restrict it.
steps: Regenerate the key in Google Cloud Console and add API and referrer restrictions.
Store it in .env only.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing.

title: Private key found in a file
description: A '-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----' block appears in a file other than the certs/ folder.
impact: A private key lets an attacker impersonate your server or decrypt traffic.

remediation.summary: Move the key to certs/ with strict permissions (or the platform's secret store) and rotate it.
steps: Remove the key from the file.
Generate a new key and certificate (npm run gen-cert or your certificate provider).
Keep private keys only in certs/ (mode 600) or a secret store.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing outside certs/.

title: JSON Web Token found in a file
description: A string shaped like a JWT (eyJ...) appears in a file.
impact: It may be a valid access token for a service; whoever has it can act as its owner until it expires.

remediation.summary: Remove the token, revoke it if possible, and never store tokens in files.
steps: Delete the token from the file.
Revoke or let it expire at the issuing service.
If tests need a token, generate one at test time.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing.

title: Random-looking value assigned to a secret-like name
description: A long, random-looking string is assigned to a variable named like key, secret, token or password.
impact: It is probably a real credential written into the code, where anyone with the code can read it.

remediation.summary: Move the value to .env and read it through config; rotate it if it was real.
steps: Confirm whether the value is a real secret.
Move it to .env and read it via config.
Rotate the credential at its provider.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing, or the finding is marked false-positive with a reason.

title: Password written in a file
description: A variable named password (or similar) is assigned a literal value.
impact: The password is visible to anyone with the code and cannot be changed without editing it.

remediation.summary: Remove the literal and read the value from .env, or generate it at runtime.
steps: Delete the literal.
If it is an account password, change the account's password.
Use config for any service credential.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing.

title: Connection string contains a password
description: A database or service URL of the form scheme://user:password@host appears in a file.
impact: Exposes the credentials for that service to anyone with the file.

remediation.summary: Move the connection string to .env and rotate the password.
steps: Remove the URL from the file.
Store it in .env and read it via config.
Change the service password.

howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan reports nothing.

title: .env is inside a git repository
description: A .env file sits next to a .git folder and is not ignored, so it may be committed.
impact: Every secret in .env becomes part of the repository history, readable by anyone with access and hard to remove.

remediation.summary: Ignore .env, remove it from history if committed, and regenerate secrets.
steps: Add .env to .gitignore.
Run git rm --cached .env if it was committed, and purge history if the repository is shared.
Run npm run setup to generate new secrets.

howToConfirmFixed: git ls-files does not list .env.

title: Known vulnerability in a dependency
description: npm audit reports a published security advisory for a package the app uses.
impact: Attackers scan for known vulnerable versions; the impact depends on the advisory and is shown with the finding.

remediation.summary: Update the package to the fixed version within the documented deadline.
steps: Read the advisory and the fixed version in the finding.
In the template repository, update package.json and package-lock.json, run the tests, and rebuild the app.
If no fix exists, check whether the vulnerable function is used and record an accepted risk with an expiry date.
remediation.example:
npm audit --json
npm update <package> --ignore-scripts

howToConfirmFixed: npm audit no longer lists the advisory.

title: No lockfile for dependencies
description: package-lock.json is missing, so installed versions are not pinned.
impact: Each install may pull newer, untested or compromised versions.

remediation.summary: Restore the tested lockfile from the template.
steps: Copy package-lock.json from templates/secure-web-app.
Install with npm ci --ignore-scripts.

howToConfirmFixed: package-lock.json exists and matches the template.

title: Dependency runs install scripts
description: A package in the lockfile declares an install script (hasInstallScript).
impact: Install scripts run arbitrary code on your computer; with ignore-scripts=true they are skipped, but the package may then not work as expected.

remediation.summary: Keep ignore-scripts=true and prefer packages without install scripts.
steps: Confirm .npmrc has ignore-scripts=true.
If the package needs its script, replace it with an alternative that does not.

howToConfirmFixed: config.ignore-scripts passes; the package is removed or accepted with a note.

title: Deprecated dependency
description: A package in use is marked deprecated by its maintainers.
impact: It will not receive security fixes; problems found later will stay unpatched.

remediation.summary: Replace it with a maintained alternative.
steps: Read the deprecation message for the recommended replacement.
Update the template dependency set and rebuild.

howToConfirmFixed: The deprecated package no longer appears in package-lock.json.

title: Copyleft licence in a dependency
description: A dependency uses a copyleft licence (for example GPL) that may impose obligations if you distribute the app.
impact: Not a security issue, but distributing the app may require releasing your source code under the same licence.

remediation.summary: Check the licence obligations or replace the package.
steps: Read the licence in the SBOM entry.
If you plan to distribute the app, ask a licensing adviser or choose an MIT/Apache alternative.

howToConfirmFixed: A recorded decision or the package replaced.

title: Software bill of materials not generated
description: The CycloneDX SBOM could not be produced (tool unavailable or lockfile unreadable).
impact: You have no inventory of the components in the app, which makes responding to new vulnerabilities slower.

remediation.summary: Restore the lockfile and re-run the dependency scan.
steps: Confirm package-lock.json exists and is valid JSON.
Re-run verification; SecureVibe falls back to building the SBOM from the lockfile.

howToConfirmFixed: reports/<run>/sbom.cdx.json exists.

title: Content Security Policy missing or weakened
description: A page response did not carry the expected Content-Security-Policy header (nonce-based script-src, object-src 'none', base-uri 'none', frame-ancestors 'none').
impact: Without this policy the browser will run any script that gets injected into a page, so a single escaping mistake becomes account takeover.

remediation.summary: Restore the template's CSP in src/security/headers.ts and remove any code that overrides it.
steps: Check that helmet is registered in src/app.ts with the buildCspDirectives policy.
Remove any res.setHeader('Content-Security-Policy', ...) overrides in feature code.
Move inline scripts to public/js/features/ with the nonce.
remediation.example: <script nonce="<%= nonce %>" src="/js/features/booking.js"></script>

howToConfirmFixed: Re-run verification; the probe passes when the header matches the exact policy.

title: HSTS header missing in TLS mode
description: With TLS_MODE set to selfsigned or proxy, responses lack Strict-Transport-Security with max-age of at least one year and includeSubDomains.
impact: Browsers may still try plain HTTP first, letting someone on the network intercept the first request.

remediation.summary: Ensure TLS_MODE is set correctly so headers.ts adds HSTS.
steps: Set TLS_MODE=proxy (behind a TLS proxy) or selfsigned.
Restart and confirm the header appears.
Behind a proxy, make sure it forwards X-Forwarded-Proto: https and TRUST_PROXY_HOPS is set.

howToConfirmFixed: curl -I https://<host>/ shows Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains.

title: X-Content-Type-Options header missing
description: A response lacked X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
impact: Browsers may guess a file's type and run an uploaded file or API response as script.

remediation.summary: Restore helmet's default headers in src/app.ts.
steps: Confirm helmet() is registered before routes and not disabled for the route.
Remove code that deletes or overrides the header.

howToConfirmFixed: Every response includes X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

title: Referrer-Policy header missing
description: A response lacked Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin.
impact: When users follow links to other sites, the full address of the page they were on (which may include ids) is sent to that site.

remediation.summary: Restore helmet's referrer policy in src/app.ts.
steps: Confirm helmet is registered with the template options.
Remove any override of Referrer-Policy.

howToConfirmFixed: Every response includes the Referrer-Policy header.

title: Content-Type without charset
description: A response with a body did not declare charset=utf-8 in its Content-Type header.
impact: Browsers may guess the character encoding, which in rare cases lets crafted text be interpreted as script.

remediation.summary: Set the Content-Type with charset on every response.
steps: Use res.json / res.render (which set charset) instead of res.send with a manual type.
If setting Content-Type by hand, include ; charset=utf-8.
remediation.example: res.type('text/plain; charset=utf-8').send(text);

howToConfirmFixed: Every response's Content-Type ends with charset=utf-8.

title: Origin header is reflected in CORS response
description: A request with a foreign Origin header received an Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing it (or *).
impact: Other websites can read responses from your app in your users' browsers, including private data.

remediation.summary: Remove CORS handling; the app serves its own pages and needs none.
steps: Delete any CORS middleware or Access-Control-* headers from the code.
If another site must call the API, use API keys and a fixed origin allow-list.

howToConfirmFixed: A request with Origin: https://evil.example gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

title: Signed-in pages are cacheable
description: A response to a signed-in user lacked Cache-Control: no-store, private.
impact: Shared computers and proxies may keep copies of private pages that the next person can open.

remediation.summary: Restore the cache-control middleware for authenticated responses.
steps: Confirm the headers middleware in src/security/headers.ts runs for authenticated routes.
Remove feature code that sets a public Cache-Control.

howToConfirmFixed: Signed-in responses carry Cache-Control: no-store, private.

title: Session cookie missing HttpOnly or SameSite=Strict
description: The session cookie was set without HttpOnly, without SameSite=Strict, or with a path other than /.
impact: Scripts could read the session, or other websites could make the browser send it, enabling session theft and cross-site request forgery.

remediation.summary: Restore the session cookie options in src/security/session.ts.
steps: Confirm the cookie is set with httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'strict', path: '/'.
Remove any code that sets the session cookie elsewhere.

howToConfirmFixed: The Set-Cookie header on login shows HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/.

title: Session cookie not Secure / not __Host- in TLS mode
description: In a TLS mode the session cookie lacked the Secure attribute or the __Host- name prefix.
impact: The cookie could be sent over plain HTTP or overwritten by another site on the same domain.

remediation.summary: Set TLS_MODE correctly so the session module names the cookie __Host-sid with Secure.
steps: Set TLS_MODE=proxy or selfsigned and TRUST_PROXY_HOPS as needed.
Confirm the proxy sends X-Forwarded-Proto: https.

howToConfirmFixed: Set-Cookie shows __Host-sid=...; Secure.

title: Old TLS version accepted
description: In selfsigned TLS mode the server accepted TLS 1.0 or 1.1.
impact: Old TLS versions have known weaknesses that let attackers on the network decrypt traffic.

remediation.summary: Restore minVersion: 'TLSv1.2' in src/server.ts TLS options.
steps: Check the https.createServer options include minVersion 'TLSv1.2'.
Behind a proxy, configure the proxy's minimum TLS version instead.

howToConfirmFixed: openssl s_client -tls1_1 fails to connect.

title: State-changing request accepted without CSRF token
description: A POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE request with a valid session but no CSRF token was accepted.
impact: Another website can make a signed-in user's browser perform actions in your app without them knowing.

remediation.summary: Ensure the route uses the default csrf: true and the form includes the token.
steps: Remove csrf: false from the route unless it is an API-key route.
Include <input type="hidden" name="_csrf" value="<%= csrfToken %>"> in the form.
Confirm the csrf middleware is registered in src/app.ts.

howToConfirmFixed: A request without the token gets 403.

title: Cross-origin request accepted
description: A state-changing request with Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site indicating another site was accepted.
impact: Other websites can trigger actions in your app on behalf of signed-in users.

remediation.summary: Restore the Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site check in src/security/csrf.ts and do not bypass it per route.
steps: Remove any code that skips the csrf middleware.
Confirm the csrf module compares Origin with the app's own origin.

howToConfirmFixed: A request with Origin: https://evil.example gets 403.

title: A GET request changes data
description: A route registered as GET created, changed or deleted data.
impact: A simple link or image tag on any site can trigger the change for a signed-in user, bypassing CSRF protection entirely.

remediation.summary: Change the route to POST (or DELETE/PUT) and submit it from a form or fetch with the CSRF token.
steps: Change method in the defineRoute spec.
Replace the link with a form that POSTs.
Update routes.manifest.json.
remediation.example: defineRoute(router, { method: 'POST', path: '/notes/:id/delete', auth: 'user', owner: { entity: 'note', param: 'id' } }, handler);

howToConfirmFixed: The probe passes: no GET route mutates state.

title: Logout does not clear browser data
description: The logout response lacked Clear-Site-Data: "cookies", "storage".
impact: Leftover cookies or storage may remain on a shared computer after sign-out.

remediation.summary: Restore the logout handler in src/features/auth to send Clear-Site-Data.
steps: Confirm the logout handler calls the headers helper that sets Clear-Site-Data.

howToConfirmFixed: The logout response includes Clear-Site-Data.

title: Hidden files are served
description: A request for /.env, /.git/config or another dotfile returned content.
impact: Secrets or source history can be downloaded by anyone.

remediation.summary: Serve static files with dotfiles: 'deny' and keep secrets outside public/.
steps: Restore express.static options in src/app.ts (dotfiles: 'deny').
Move any dotfiles out of public/.

howToConfirmFixed: Requests for /.env and /.git/config return 404.

title: Directory listing exposed
description: Requesting a folder path returned a list of files.
impact: Attackers learn the names of every file, including ones you did not intend to publish.

remediation.summary: Disable directory indexes in the static middleware.
steps: Restore express.static with index: false and no serve-index middleware.

howToConfirmFixed: Requesting /css/ returns 404.

title: HTTP TRACE is supported
description: A TRACE request was not refused with 405.
impact: TRACE echoes request headers and can be abused to read cookies in some setups.

remediation.summary: Restore the TRACE rejection in src/app.ts.
steps: Confirm the method filter that returns 405 for TRACE is registered before routes.

howToConfirmFixed: curl -X TRACE returns 405.

title: Health endpoint reveals internal details
description: /healthz or /readyz returned more than a status word (versions, hostnames, database paths), or /readyz answered a non-loopback request.
impact: Attackers learn about your setup for free, and a public readiness probe can be used to map your infrastructure.

remediation.summary: Return only {"status":"ok"} from /healthz and keep /readyz loopback-only.
steps: Restore the health handlers in src/server.ts.
Do not add extra fields to the health response.

howToConfirmFixed: /healthz returns exactly {"status":"ok"}.

title: Test-mode endpoints reachable in production
description: In production mode, /__securevibe/routes or another test helper endpoint responded instead of returning 404.
impact: Test mode seeds known accounts and exposes internal routes; in production this is a back door.

remediation.summary: Ensure test mode only activates with NODE_ENV=test and SECUREVIBE_TEST_MODE=1 and that .env does not set them.
steps: Remove SECUREVIBE_TEST_MODE from .env.
Restore src/config.ts and src/app.ts from the template if modified.
Delete seeded @test.local accounts.

howToConfirmFixed: /__securevibe/routes returns 404 in production mode.

title: Health endpoint not working
description: /healthz did not return 200 with {"status":"ok"}.
impact: Monitoring tools cannot tell whether the app is up, delaying detection of outages.

remediation.summary: Restore the /healthz handler in src/server.ts.
steps: Confirm the handler is registered and not blocked by auth or rate limits.

howToConfirmFixed: /healthz returns 200 with {"status":"ok"}.

title: Readiness endpoint not working or exposed
description: /readyz did not return {"status":"ready"} from loopback, or answered a non-loopback request without BIND_LAN.
impact: Operators cannot tell whether the app can serve traffic, or internal readiness details are exposed to the network.

remediation.summary: Restore the /readyz handler with its loopback check.
steps: Confirm the handler checks the database connection and restricts to 127.0.0.1 unless BIND_LAN=1.

howToConfirmFixed: /readyz returns {"status":"ready"} locally and 404/403 remotely.

title: Error response contains technical details
description: An error response contained a stack trace, file path, SQL text or secret-looking value.
impact: Technical details help attackers find weaknesses and may leak data directly.

remediation.summary: Restore the generic error handler in src/app.ts and never send err.message to clients.
steps: Confirm the final error handler returns the uniform error model.
Remove res.send(err) or res.json(err) from feature code; log with logger.error instead.

howToConfirmFixed: Error responses contain only the generic message.

title: Not-found page leaks details
description: The 404 response echoed the requested path unescaped or revealed framework details.
impact: Echoing the path can enable reflected script injection; framework details help attackers.

remediation.summary: Restore the template's 404 handler and page.
steps: Confirm the 404 handler renders views/errors/404.ejs without the raw path.

howToConfirmFixed: A request for /<script>x</script> returns a plain 404 page.

title: Server error page leaks details
description: A forced server error returned a stack trace or Express default error page.
impact: Internal structure and possibly data are exposed to anyone who can trigger an error.

remediation.summary: Restore the template's error handler and ensure NODE_ENV is production.
steps: Confirm the error handler in src/app.ts is the last middleware.
Set NODE_ENV=production.

howToConfirmFixed: A forced error returns the generic error page with a request id only.

title: Wrong HTTP method not rejected cleanly
description: Sending an unsupported method to a route produced a 500 or unexpected behaviour instead of 404/405.
impact: Unexpected methods may reach code paths that were never meant to be reachable.

remediation.summary: Register routes with explicit methods and let the router return 404/405 for others.
steps: Do not use router.all or app.use for feature handlers.
Confirm each defineRoute has a single method.

howToConfirmFixed: Unsupported methods return 404 or 405.

title: Oversized request body accepted
description: A request body larger than the configured limit was not rejected with 413.
impact: Large bodies consume memory and can be used to slow or crash the app.

remediation.summary: Restore the body limits in src/app.ts.
steps: Confirm express.json({ limit }) and express.urlencoded({ limit }) use the template limits.
Do not add a route-level parser with a larger limit.

howToConfirmFixed: A 2 MB JSON body to an API route returns 413.

title: Duplicate parameters accepted
description: A request with the same parameter twice was processed instead of rejected.
impact: Parameter pollution can confuse validation and lead to the wrong value being used.

remediation.summary: Keep the 'simple' query parser and strict schemas that reject arrays for scalars.
steps: Confirm app.set('query parser', 'simple') in src/app.ts.
Use validateQuery helpers that reject arrays where a string is expected.

howToConfirmFixed: A request with ?id=1&id=2 returns 400.

title: __proto__ in input not rejected
description: A JSON body containing __proto__ or constructor.prototype keys was accepted.
impact: Crafted input may alter the behaviour of all objects in the process, bypassing checks or crashing the app.

remediation.summary: Use strict zod schemas (unknown keys rejected) and the template's prototype-pollution guard in src/app.ts.
steps: Confirm the JSON body guard middleware is registered.
Mark every body schema .strict().

howToConfirmFixed: A body with {"__proto__":{"x":1}} returns 400.

title: Unknown field accepted
description: A request with an extra, undeclared field was accepted instead of rejected with 400.
impact: Users may set fields they should not control (mass assignment), such as role or owner.

remediation.summary: Declare a strict schema for the route.
steps: Add .strict() to the body schema in the defineRoute spec.
Read only req.valid.body.
remediation.example: schema: { body: z.object({ title: z.string().max(120) }).strict() }

howToConfirmFixed: A body with an extra field returns 400 with code validation_error.

title: Wrong-typed input accepted
description: A request that sent an array or object where a string or number was expected was processed.
impact: Code that assumes a type may behave unpredictably, skipping checks or crashing.

remediation.summary: Use the typed zod schema for every parameter and reject arrays for scalars.
steps: Declare z.string() / z.number().int() with limits for each field.
Use the validate helpers from src/security/validate.ts.

howToConfirmFixed: A request with name[]=x returns 400.

title: SQL-style input caused a server error
description: Sending ' or " OR 1=1-- in a string parameter produced a 500 error, which suggests the value reached a query unsafely.
impact: A crafted value may be able to read or change other data (SQL injection).

remediation.summary: Use db helpers with ? placeholders for the affected route and add input limits.
steps: Find the route from the finding and locate its query.
Replace string concatenation with parameters.
Add a max length to the schema.
remediation.example: db.all('SELECT id, name FROM customers WHERE name LIKE ? AND owner_id = ? LIMIT 50', [`%${q}%`, req.user.id]);

howToConfirmFixed: The same input now returns 200 or 400, never 500, and the static scan is clean.

title: Path traversal input not rejected
description: A path parameter containing ../ was not rejected with 400 or 404.
impact: The value may reach the file system and read or write files outside the intended folder.

remediation.summary: Validate path parameters as ids and never use them in file paths.
steps: Use an id schema (uuid or integer) for :param values.
Look files up by database id; see the uploads module.
remediation.example: schema: { params: z.object({ id: z.string().uuid() }).strict() }

howToConfirmFixed: A request with ../ in the path returns 400 or 404.

title: Session id appears in a URL
description: A session identifier was found in a redirect location, link or query string.
impact: URLs are logged and shared; a session id in a URL lets whoever sees it take over the session.

remediation.summary: Keep the session only in the cookie; never add it to links or redirects.
steps: Search for sid or session in URL-building code and remove it.
Rely on the cookie set by src/security/session.ts.

howToConfirmFixed: No response or page contains the session id outside Set-Cookie.

title: Session id too short or predictable
description: The session cookie value is shorter than 43 base64url characters (32 random bytes) or not random.
impact: Short or predictable ids can be guessed, letting an attacker hijack sessions.

remediation.summary: Restore session id generation with crypto.randomBytes(32) in src/security/session.ts.
steps: Confirm randomBytes(32).toString('base64url') is used.
Remove any custom session cookie code.

howToConfirmFixed: The session cookie is 43 characters of base64url and differs each login.

title: Session id not changed at login
description: The session cookie value before and after signing in was the same.
impact: An attacker who planted a session id in a victim's browser (session fixation) shares the victim's signed-in session.

remediation.summary: Call session.regenerate on successful login and MFA verification.
steps: Confirm the login handler calls the session module's rotate/regenerate function.
Do not reuse the anonymous session after authentication.

howToConfirmFixed: The cookie value changes on login.

title: Session still valid after logout
description: A request using the old session cookie after logout was treated as signed in.
impact: Anyone who copied the cookie can keep using the account after the user signed out.

remediation.summary: Invalidate the session row on logout in src/features/auth.
steps: Confirm logout calls the session store's revoke for the current id.
Confirm the middleware checks revoked_at and expires_at.

howToConfirmFixed: A request with the old cookie after logout is treated as anonymous.

title: No visible logout on a signed-in page
description: An authenticated page did not contain the logout form from the base layout.
impact: Users on shared computers may not sign out, leaving their session open.

remediation.summary: Render generated pages with the base layout that includes the logout form.
steps: Use layouts/base.ejs for every page.
Do not remove the logout partial.

howToConfirmFixed: Every signed-in page shows the logout button.

title: Protected route reachable without signing in
description: A route declared as requiring sign-in responded to an anonymous request with data or success.
impact: Anyone on the network can read or change data without an account.

remediation.summary: Ensure the route is registered with defineRoute and auth 'user' or 'role:<name>', and that requireAuth is not bypassed.
steps: Check the route's auth value in the defineRoute spec and routes.manifest.json.
Remove any early response before the auth middleware runs.
remediation.example: defineRoute(router, { method: 'GET', path: '/api/invoices', auth: 'user' }, handler);

howToConfirmFixed: An anonymous request returns 401 (API) or redirects to sign-in (page).

title: Route reachable by the wrong role
description: A route restricted to a role (for example admin) responded successfully to a user with another role.
impact: Staff or customers can use administrator functions such as managing users or exporting data.

remediation.summary: Set auth: 'role:admin' (or the correct roles list) on the route.
steps: Fix the auth/roles value in the defineRoute spec.
Add a test that the wrong role gets 403.
